name: Netskope
evidence_summary: Netskope source evidences acquisition of Infiot to deliver integrated single-vendor SASE and Borderless WAN for enterprise locations/cloud.
cost_model: Quote-based subscription; modules commonly priced by users, sites, traffic and security functions.
key_differentiators: Strong CASB heritage; widely recognised as a leading SSE vendor for SaaS-heavy environments.
Borderless WAN (from the Infiot acquisition) extends Netskope into single-vendor SASE for buyers wanting both layers from one platform.
Detailed SaaS application visibility and policy controls.
best_fit_for: Enterprises with deep SaaS adoption where CASB and DLP are top procurement priorities.
Buyers comparing single-vendor SASE platforms after starting with SSE.
Organisations selecting Netskope SSE alongside a separate SD-WAN platform via partner integration.
watch_outs: Native SD-WAN (Borderless WAN) is newer than dedicated SD-WAN platforms; validate path selection and QoS depth in RFP.
Managed delivery is partner-led; first-party managed service is limited.
Premium pricing with modular structure; full SASE bundle costs can scale meaningfully with users and traffic.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: SkopeAI for data and threat protection; UEBA analytics across users and apps.

resilience.note: NewEdge private cloud runs full compute in every region; localised failover.

profile.platform_architecture: Netskope One runs on NewEdge, a private security cloud where every region runs full compute for every service, keeping inspection close to users without backhaul. The platform was built data-first: the Zero Trust Engine inspects traffic and content in a single pass with rich app and instance awareness. Netskope also fields its own Borderless SD-WAN (from the Infiot acquisition), making it one of the few SSE leaders with a first-party WAN edge.
profile.security_sase: CASB is where Netskope made its name and it remains the reference: granular SaaS app instance control, inline and API modes, with DLP depth to match. SWG, ZTNA (Private Access) and FWaaS complete the SSE set, with SkopeAI covering AI app governance and shadow AI discovery. For cloud-heavy, data-sensitive estates the control granularity is the differentiator.
profile.service_support_channel: UK presence is strong, with managed offers through security MSPs and carriers. Deployment uses agents and IPsec/GRE feeds with substantial migration tooling. Support runs to 24x7 with professional services; like its SSE peers, policy excellence rewards skilled ownership.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-user subscription licensing, quote based, premium positioned alongside Zscaler. The Netify verdict: shortlist Netskope when SaaS and data governance lead: instance-level CASB control, top-tier DLP and AI app governance are the strongest cards. Its first-party SD-WAN makes single-vendor SASE plausible; many buyers still pair NewEdge with established SD-WAN vendors.

vendor_faqs.q: What makes Netskope CASB stand out?
vendor_faqs.a: Instance awareness: Netskope distinguishes corporate from personal instances of the same SaaS app and applies different policy to each, with deep activity-level controls and DLP inline. For unsanctioned app governance it remains the benchmark.

vendor_faqs.q: Does Netskope offer SD-WAN as well as SSE?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes, Borderless SD-WAN from the Infiot acquisition: lightweight edges managed in the same Netskope One console, making single-vendor SASE viable. Validate routing depth against network-heritage rivals for complex topologies.

vendor_faqs.q: How does NewEdge differ from running security in hyperscale clouds?
vendor_faqs.a: NewEdge is Netskope's own infrastructure with full service compute in every region, extensive peering and published latency commitments, designed to avoid hairpinning and keep single-pass inspection close to the user.

shortlist_summary: Netskope are widely recognised as a leading SSE vendor, particularly for SaaS-heavy environments, with CASB heritage that few competitors match. Typically shortlisted as the security component in a best-of-breed SASE architecture alongside a separate SD-WAN platform, rather than as a single-vendor SD-WAN replacement. The shortlist score reflects SSE depth rather than SD-WAN breadth, which is consistent with how Netskope is most commonly deployed.
cost_note: Per-user subscription, premium-adjacent but mid versus the most expensive SSE leaders.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK NewEdge presence; delivered direct or via UK security MSPs.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: build managed SASE services around Netskope's platform
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Netskope's own customer-facing pages describe professional services, technical support and customer success, not end-to-end design, operate, monitor and change management of a customer's service. Named-author trade coverage of the Catalyst programme frames managed SASE as something MSP partners build and deliver on the Netskope platform. Graded managed_service_dependent rather than yes because the operating party is a partner, not Netskope.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: build managed SASE services around Netskope's platform
f03_co_managed_service.note: No page reviewed uses co-managed language or sets out a split of policy and change rights between Netskope and the customer. Netskope runs the SaaS platform and offers tiered support with technical account management at Premium Plus level, but the shared-responsibility model is not documented. Where a co-managed arrangement exists it appears to sit with an MSP partner rather than Netskope. Low confidence.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: A self-service multi-tenant orchestrator for the full SASE and AI product suite that quickly provisions production-ready customer environments.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Multi-tenant provisioning and delegated administration across unlimited partner tiers are documented in the June 2026 Catalyst announcement and corroborated by ChannelE2E. Branded or white-label partner portals and reusable customer templates were not evidenced on any page read, so graded partial rather than yes.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Smooth migration onto advanced Netskope platform
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: The professional services page documents implementation, migration from siloed legacy solutions, tailored statements of work for complex enterprise deployments, service packages and training. Discovery, pilot, runbook and rollback detail is not itemised on the public page.

f07_lifecycle_management.note: The SD-WAN datasheet documents zero-touch activation and one-click hardware RMA, and the platform is cloud-managed from a single console. No page read states that firmware upgrades, patching, renewals or end-of-life planning are performed as part of the service, so graded partial rather than yes.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Reliable, high-performance 5G connectivity for primary, backup, or active-active links delivers sub-second brownout/blackout protection.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: 5G Standalone is supported as primary, backup or active-active transport. eSIM with on-gateway LPAd covers SIM management, the Converged Gateway carries built-in 4G/5G with Netskope Zero Trust SIM across 400+ networks, and digital experience management reports cellular signal strength and quality.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Unlike vendors that rely on the public cloud, Netskope has complete control over its NewEdge infrastructure
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: NewEdge is Netskope's own security cloud, presented as full-compute data centres carrying the complete SSE stack, expressly contrasted with vendors hosting on third-party public cloud. This is the vendor's own service infrastructure, so yes rather than partner_integrated.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: Embedded Data Planes provide fully private, dedicated deployments with full compute and a complete SASE stack
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: The March 2026 NewEdge datasheet documents Embedded Data Planes as fully private, dedicated deployments, alongside 12+ NewEdge management planes across 8 countries for sovereignty. The May 2026 sovereignty release adds in-country processing and domestic storage. Whether Embedded Data Planes can be hosted on customer premises is not stated, hence medium confidence.

f21_private_global_backbone.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The NewEdge product page and the March 2026 NewEdge datasheet were read specifically for this. Both describe a purpose-built private security cloud with dense peering, presence in 120+ internet exchanges and nearly 11,000 adjacencies to 750+ ASNs, but neither states that inter-region traffic between PoPs rides a Netskope-owned or Netskope-controlled backbone. Absence of a statement is not treated as evidence of absence, so recorded as unknown.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: Netskope launches an industry-first SLA committing to less than 50 ms of latency for processing encrypted traffic
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Contractual commitments cover uptime and availability at five nines plus latency for both decrypted and non-decrypted traffic. The NewEdge datasheet repeats industry-best SLAs for availability and latency. Support response-time and change-handling commitments sit in Support Terms, which were not reachable in this task.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Netskope IPS scans network traffic to find and prevent vulnerability exploits
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Firewall as a Service is Netskope's own technology delivered from NewEdge data centres with application-aware firewall rules and native IPS, on one platform, console, policy engine and client. Web categorisation across 130+ categories, anti-malware with multi-stage sandboxing and single-pass TLS inspection are documented on the Next Gen SWG page within the same platform. The phrase stateful firewall was not found verbatim on the pages read, hence medium confidence.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Alert and coach users on data loss risks, including app and user risk context, when performing activities.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Content is classified and inspected for PII, payment card and financial data and intellectual property, with real-time coaching, a proceed or cancel option and end-to-end incident workflows or third-party integrations.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: We are a global team and operate 24/7/365
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Netskope runs a global support organisation on a 24/7/365 basis at Premium and Premium Plus tiers, with technical account management and a focused technical support engineer at Premium Plus. No page read describes a Netskope NOC or SOC proactively monitoring the customer service, owning incidents through to root cause analysis, or running structured service reviews and change governance, so graded partial.

delivery_model.quote: build managed SASE services around Netskope's platform
delivery_model.note: Netskope authors and operates the Netskope One SASE/SSE platform and the NewEdge cloud, and sells professional services and tiered technical support. Managed service delivery to end customers is described as something MSP partners build on the platform, not something Netskope itself operates end to end.

underlay_ownership.quote: Present in 120+ internet exchanges with deep peering to ISPs, CDNs, cloud, and SaaS providers
underlay_ownership.note: Netskope owns and controls its NewEdge compute and core routing and runs its own peering at 120+ internet exchanges, but the pages read describe reaching customers and SaaS over peering and third-party ISP transit rather than owning physical circuits. Branch and user access circuits are customer supplied. No page reviewed states that Netskope owns fibre or long-haul capacity.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: FWaaS is available globally via NewEdge data centers
sse_layer_ownership.note: The secure web gateway, firewall as a service, IPS, threat protection and DLP are Netskope-authored modules on the Netskope One platform, delivered from Netskope's own NewEdge cloud. No third-party security vendor is named as supplying the enforcement stack on any page read.

regulatory_documentation.quote: Netskope System & Organization Control (SOC) Reports are independent third-party examination reports
regulatory_documentation.note: Found named on the compliance page: AICPA SOC 2 reports, the California Consumer Privacy Act, CIS, and a FedRAMP High authorisation reference. Not found on any page read: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2. ISO 27001 and ISO 27018 are claimed in a separate Netskope press release surfaced in search but not fetched in this task, so they are not counted here. The compliance page body was truncated on fetch, so the full framework list may be longer than recorded; confidence medium for that reason.

pop_count.quote: Powered by 120+ data centers in 80+ regions today, including Mainland China
pop_count.note: Published as 120+ data centres across 80+ regions, with Localization Zones extending coverage to 220+ countries and territories. The March 2026 datasheet and the May 2026 sovereignty press release give the same 120+ and 80+ figures. The figure is a floor, not an exact count.

sla_availability_pct.note: Published as a five-nines uptime and availability SLA, alongside separate latency SLAs of under 10 milliseconds for non-decrypted traffic and under 50 milliseconds for encrypted traffic processing. The full SLA contract text was not reachable, so the percentage rests on the supplier press release.

sectors.healthcare.quote: Netskope helps healthcare organizations maintain patient privacy, secure organizational IP, avoid regulatory fines, guard against data breaches, and provide optimized, zero trust access to people, devices, and data anywhere they go.
sectors.healthcare.note: Graded yes on the dedicated industry page test, not on a customer. There is no named healthcare case study anywhere I could reach, and the page's HIPAA and HITECH language describes helping customers comply rather than any accreditation Netskope itself holds. Elevance Health appears as a logo on the customers page but with no linked story behind it, so it corroborates rather than proves. The UK public sector page separately names the NHS as one of five focus areas.

sectors.financial_services.quote: More than 4,000 customers, including three of the five largest financial services companies on the Fortune 100, trust our unified secure access service edge (SASE) platform, Netskope One.
sectors.financial_services.note: The best evidenced sector by a clear margin. Four named customer stories on the industry page (Apex Group, JLL, RSM Australia, Ascensus), plus BMO and The Auto Club Group as logos, plus explicit DORA, GDPR, NIS 2 and PCI references. The Fortune 100 claim is a vendor claim and is not independently verified here.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Dedicated industry page, which meets the yes test, and two named retail logos on the customers page (Ross Stores, Sainsburys Supermarkets Ltd). Confidence is medium rather than high because the page carries no named retail case study; its only testimonial is anonymised as 'SOC Analyst, Fortune 500 Retailer'. The case studies index is client side rendered so a named retail study may exist that I could not retrieve.

sectors.manufacturing.quote: Netskope helps the world's largest and most demanding manufacturing companies securely adopt the cloud to streamline operations and compete at all levels.
sectors.manufacturing.note: Dedicated industry page plus an unusually strong set of manufacturer logos on the customers page: Airbus, Yamaha Motor Corporation, Colgate Palmolive, AVX Corporation and Orbia. No named manufacturing case study; the page testimonial is anonymised as 'Security Architect, Fortune 100 Equipment Manufacturer'.

sectors.energy_utilities.note: Dedicated industry page and one named customer, PDC Energy. Note the page is framed around utilities and billing rather than OT or ICS security, so it evidences the sector but not necessarily operational technology capability. Republic Services appears as a logo on the customers page but is waste services rather than energy, so I have not counted it.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Netskope GovCloud holds FedRAMP High Authorization, the maximum cloud security certification level available.
sectors.government_public_sector.note: The strongest accreditation backed sector. Four separate government pages (US federal, US state and local, UK, Australia), FedRAMP High for GovCloud, an IRAP assessment to PROTECTED for Australia, and an attributed quote from Gary Stevens, Deputy CIO and Director of Cyber Strategy at the Department of Veterans Affairs. ManTech International, a defence contractor, appears both on the federal page and as a customer logo. No StateRAMP status was found on the state and local page.

sectors.education.quote: Netskope enables K12 schools to use the cloud and web securely.
sectors.education.note: Two dedicated industry pages, Higher Education and K12, which meets the yes test, and education is named as one of five UK public sector focus areas. Confidence is medium because neither page names a single university, college or school district, and no education case study was retrievable. This is a sector Netskope addresses on paper more clearly than it demonstrates with customers.

sectors.transport_logistics.note: No evidence found and I am confident the absence is real, not a search failure. I checked the full solutions index, which lists fifteen industry pages and includes no transport or logistics entry; I fetched /solutions/transportation-and-logistics directly and got a 404; I read the Service Companies page specifically for transport, logistics, shipping or airline content and found none; and I scanned the press release index for logistics customers. Prologis appears as a customer logo and is often read as logistics, but it is a logistics real estate owner with no linked case study, and inferring sector capability from a single unexplained logo is exactly the reasoning this exercise is meant to remove.

sectors.professional_services.quote: BDO Brings Together Networking and Security to Protect a Cloud-First, AI-Friendly Infrastructure
sectors.professional_services.note: The only fully named and linked case study on the site, labelled by Netskope with the industry 'Business Services' and located in London, UK. Reinforced by two further industry pages (Legal, Service Companies), a named customer on each of them in Oak Hill Advisors and the RSM Australia story, and law firm BLG plus JLL as logos.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: Graded partial rather than yes deliberately. Hospitality has no page of its own; it is named in the title of a shared retail page whose body content, use cases and single testimonial are all retail. There is no hospitality customer, no hospitality case study and no hospitality specific compliance content. This is the sector named in a heading with nothing behind it, which is the partial test. A reviewer applying the dedicated page rule mechanically would reach yes, so I am flagging the disagreement rather than hiding it.

regions.uk_ireland.quote: powered by full compute data centres in multiple UK cities
regions.uk_ireland.note: Specific in country infrastructure claim rather than a global one, supported by a London based named case study (BDO) and by four UK reseller listings on the Crown Commercial Service Digital Marketplace whose data storage and processing fields name the United Kingdom. Ireland specifically is not mentioned anywhere I read; the evidence is UK only and the region grade carries Ireland by grouping, not by evidence.

regions.europe.note: Confidence is medium because the cleanest evidence is third party rather than from Netskope. The Somerford and Integrity360 G-Cloud listings both declare data storage and processing locations including the European Economic Area with user control over location, which is a delivery statement on a binding public register. Netskope's own site gave me nothing Europe specific: /solutions/dora-compliance, /solutions/nis2-compliance and /solutions/gdpr all returned 404, and the NewEdge page publishes only aggregate figures with no European city list. Raiffeisen Information Service and GBfoods are named or logoed European customers, which corroborates.

regions.north_america.quote: Netskope GovCloud holds FedRAMP High Authorization, the maximum cloud security certification level available.
regions.north_america.note: FedRAMP High is a US government authorisation that cannot be held without US based, assessed infrastructure, so it evidences delivery rather than presence. Reinforced by the Santa Clara headquarters, a US federal agency customer quote, and BMO plus The Auto Club Group as North American customer logos.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: Netskope has been independently assessed under the Information Security Registered Assessors Program (IRAP) to the PROTECTED level.
regions.asia_pacific.note: The Australian Government page names three in country data plane locations, Sydney, Melbourne and Perth, and cites an IRAP assessment to PROTECTED. IRAP is an Australian Government scheme carried out by registered assessors, so this is the one regional claim with genuine independent backing. RSM Australia is a named customer story on the financial services page. Evidence is heavily Australia weighted; Japan, Singapore, India and the rest of Asia Pacific are covered only by the aggregate NewEdge figure.

regions.middle_east_africa.note: No region specific evidence found. The only applicable material is the aggregate NewEdge claim of 120+ data centres in 80+ regions and Localization Zones reaching 220+ countries and territories, which almost certainly includes this region but names no city, country or point of presence in it. Under the rule that this field measures service delivery and not a global marketing figure, that is not gradeable. I checked the NewEdge platform page, the NewEdge blog tag and the press release index for Middle East or Africa locations and found none, and the /netskope-newedge path that may hold a per city list is blocked by robots.txt.

regions.latin_america.note: Same position as Middle East and Africa: only the aggregate 80+ regions and 220+ countries and territories figures, with no Latin American city, country or point of presence published. Orbia is a Mexico headquartered customer logo and GBfoods has Latin American operations, but neither has a linked case study and a logo does not evidence in region service delivery. Recorded as unknown rather than inferred.

regions.china_mainland.quote: 120+ data centers in 80+ regions today, including Mainland China
regions.china_mainland.note: This is the rare case where the China test is actually met. Netskope does not rely on a generic global claim: it calls out Mainland China explicitly in the coverage sentence, states full compute and all SASE services at the edge in every location, and maintains a separate named NewEdge China solution described as providing specialised, compliant access to domestic or international apps with its own datasheet. What is not published, and what a buyer should still ask for, is the licensing basis and the operating partner, since a foreign provider cannot deliver in country without a licensed arrangement.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: More than 4,000 customers, including three of the five largest financial services companies on the Fortune 100, trust our unified secure access service edge (SASE) platform, Netskope One.
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Unambiguous and corroborated across three separate pages. The investor relations site states thousands of customers including more than 30 of the Fortune 100, and the company page repeats 30%+ Fortune 100. The customer logo set is almost entirely global enterprise: Airbus, BMO, Colgate Palmolive, Elevance Health, Yamaha Motor Corporation. Netskope is NASDAQ listed as NTSK, so the investor relations version of this claim carries securities law accountability rather than being pure marketing.

organisation_fit.mid_market.note: No explicit mid market targeting found. I read the partners page and the June 2026 Catalyst MSP/SP programme press release specifically looking for mid market, SMB or segment language and neither uses those terms. The MSP and service provider route to market and the per user G-Cloud pricing with no stated minimum commitment would both suit mid market buyers, but that is inference about what could work rather than evidence of who Netskope targets, so it does not carry a grade. A buyer in this bracket should treat mid market fit as an open question to put to the vendor.

organisation_fit.small_business.note: No evidence either way. There is no published SMB tier, no self serve sign up, no free tier and no pricing page at all on netskope.com, and the partners page carries no small business language. Everything readable points at enterprise, but Netskope nowhere states that small business is out of scope, so not_primary would be over reading it. Unknown is the honest grade.

published_pricing.note: Netskope publishes no pricing itself; /products/netskope-one/pricing returns 404 and no entry point appears anywhere on the site. The grade rests entirely on four independent UK Digital Marketplace reseller listings, which are binding published prices on a government procurement register. They cluster tightly: £111.62 a user a year (Somerford Associates), £130 a user a year (ITHQ), £9.00 a unit a month, which is £108 a year (Bytes Software Services), and £8.10 a unit (Integrity360). Roughly £108 to £130 per user per year for SSE sits in the middle of this market, hence mid rather than premium or value. Two caveats a buyer should weigh: these are reseller packages for public sector framework buyers, not Netskope list price, and the underlying module mix differs between listings, so they are not strictly like for like. Enterprise direct pricing at Fortune 100 scale is unpublished and may sit anywhere.
